title: Maintenance Due Calculator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Operating a Robot Arm
description: Move three sliders to see when a maintenance task becomes due: the hours of use now, the hours at which the task was last done, and its interval. Then solve six problems about hours left, percent used and weeks until due. Used in Chapter 18.

educational.topic: Maintenance schedules counted in hours of use
learningObjectives: Calculate the hours left before a maintenance task is due, the percent of its interval used, and the weeks until it is due, to within 0.1 of the unit shown, in six problems, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Choose and use one of a few formulas on new numbers again and again, with the correct value and the working shown after each commit
keyQuestions: How many hours has the arm run since the task was last done?
What does a negative number of hours left mean?
commonMisconceptions: The interval is counted in calendar days
Hours left is the interval minus the hours now
An overdue task has zero hours left
assessmentOpportunities: Six committed answers, each within 0.1 of the correct value; 5 of 6 for mastery

controls.label: Last done at
controls.range: 0 to 200 hours, step 1, default 30 (never more than the hours now)

controls.label: Your answer
controls.range: a number in the unit shown; negative when a task is overdue

controls.label: Start / Check / Next problem / See score / Try again
